output.brief: The wrong expiry dates did not come from the agency operators. The printer records show that from 4 Oct (22:10) every Veltranol job received a 36-month shelf life from the line integration service, and no job was overridden. The pre-October jobs, including agency-operator jobs after the firmware change, were correct. On 3 Oct, Regulatory Affairs entered a 36-month value for Veltranol that is valid only from 1 Mar 2027. The 24-month value is still the one in effect. Something is reading that future-dated value early. The vendor says this shouldn't happen, so that is the point to confirm. Two Line 1 day-shift lots from permanent staff are also affected and sit in the warehouse. The camera only checks the print against the job data, so it passed them all. Warnings and removing the agency staff would punish the wrong people and leave the fault in place. Do now: reset the Veltranol shelf-life record. Hold every Veltranol lot packed since 4 Oct, including the two Line 1 lots. Add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record at each setup. Check retained cartons of the two other products with future-dated edits (HX-15-30, MR-05-14). Ask Corvane and IT why the future-dated value was used. Don't relabel other products or switch off the camera check. A 12-month site-wide reconciliation can wait until those checks show a wider problem. I'm fairly confident in the cause. Other products are unchecked.
